### 🧪 NetSpeedTray 2.2.1-beta.1

The first beta of 2.2.1, the first patch after 2.2.0. Thanks for trying it early.

**Betas don't update in-app, and WinGet and the Store won't offer this one.** Download Setup.exe or the portable zip below and install over 2.2.0 as usual. Your history and settings carry over. When 2.2.1 final ships, your beta offers it through the normal in-app update.

### What's in this beta

- **Every GPU in the hover card.** On a PC with two or more, each gets its own usage, temperature, power and memory. The taskbar still shows one.
- **Hybrid (Optimus) laptops:** NetSpeedTray no longer wakes a sleeping NVIDIA GPU just to read its temperature. Temperature and power show "—" while it sleeps.
- **A 0.5 s update rate, if you want it.** "Real-time (0.5s)" on the Update rate slider. 1 s stays the default, now called "Standard (1s)".
- **Update offers no longer open a window on their own.** The app now also checks while it keeps running, and offers a new version with a small notice by the widget. "Not now" in the update window holds that version back for 3 days.
- **RAM and VRAM on their own**, without CPU or GPU monitoring.
- **Line spacing** for the two speed rows (Settings → Appearance), counted from the default. Thanks @pasharm.
- **Bengali digits** in fixed text, and Monitor graphs drawn in Bengali.
- **Choose what the right-click menu shows** (Settings → General). Thanks @kamal63442 for the idea.
- **Fewer wake-ups at idle**, for battery: the background threads no longer wake every tenth of a second to check for work.
- **Stricter in-app updates:** the installer must match the release's published checksums (thanks @kamal63442), and a portable update checks every file it installs, not just NetSpeedTray.exe.
- **The Wi-Fi name without Location access.** Thanks @XYuki-cloud.
- Fixes: the widget goes back onto the taskbar after Windows moves it (Remote Desktop), a new update rate applies at once, the widget no longer sits on a Windows 10 taskbar's Desktop/Links toolbars, with "Hide while app buttons cover the widget" off it moves to the spot by the tray when that's clear, Check connection pings your real router with a VPN up, "Above <throttle> for" is right on long windows, and a CPU/GPU label color you picked stays that color on an accent-colored taskbar (Settings now says when the accent color makes one of your other colors too faint).

### What I'd love you to test

- **Hybrid / Optimus laptops** (@balciseri): does the NVIDIA GPU get to sleep now, on battery and on AC? Do temperature and power come back when a game or video wakes it?
- **Two or more GPUs:** is every GPU in the hover card, with the right numbers next to the right name?
- **0.5 s** (@evandrosergiooliveira-cloud): does it feel like the old 1.2.4 rate? Any CPU cost you notice?
- **Bengali** (@Askeleid): the digits, the Monitor graphs, and the new line-spacing strings.
- **The update notice:** when 2.2.1 final is out, the beta offers it with the notice instead of a window. Did it show up, and did it get in your way?
- **Windows 10 / ExplorerPatcher taskbar with the Desktop or Links toolbar** (@Achaean): does the widget sit left of it, and does a dragged widget stay put?
- **Remote Desktop** (@bobbergen): if you remote into a PC running it, does the widget stay on the taskbar?
- **Accent-colored taskbar:** are your custom CPU/GPU label colors kept, and does Settings show a note when one of your other colors is too faint?
- **Portable:** does the zip start and keep your settings? The update from this beta to 2.2.1 final is the first one that checks every file, so portable users, please take that update in-app and tell me how it went.

### Translators

The new and reworded strings are machine-drafted in every language. The list is in #364, and corrections there are very welcome. 2.2.1 final waits at least a week so there's time for them.

### What's next

2.2.1 final, after this beta has been tested and translators have had at least a week.

Found something? Open a new issue, or comment on #NNN, with a support bundle (Export support bundle at the bottom of Settings). Usernames, paths and IPs are stripped from it.
